title: Norfolk named one of the most haunted places in the UK

Headless ghosts, haunted castles and unexplained sightings have earned Norfolk a spot among the most haunted places in the UK.

Travel specialists Ski Vertigo compiled the rankings using data from the Paranormal Database, which records sightings, folklore and historical accounts of ghosts and hauntings across the country.

Reports of UFOs, big cats or other supernatural creatures were not included.

Each county is listed with its number of ghost reports and one of its best-known haunted places.

Norfolk ranks tenth with 293 recorded ghost reports, with Norwich topping the county’s list at 26 sightings, followed by King’s Lynn with 17 and Great Yarmouth with 12.

Blickling Hall is on the site of Anne Boleyn's family's former home (Image: Newsquest / Danielle Booden)

Blickling Hall is one of Norfolk’s most famous haunted locations, said to be visited by the headless ghost of Anne Boleyn each year on May 19, the anniversary of her death.

Essex claimed the top spot with 422 ghost reports.

Other counties on the list include Sussex with 404, Kent with 374 and Suffolk with 350.

London was not ranked due to the database categorising reports by postcode rather than county.
